3	## Packages
4	
5	- `config` reads the environment once at start-up and validates it. Every
6	  knob has a default in `config.Defaults`; `Load` never reads the

9	  `MemStore`, a mutex-guarded map. Items are copied in and out, so callers
10	  cannot mutate stored state through a returned value.
11	- `server` builds the HTTP mux over a `Store`. Handlers are methods on
12	  `Server` so they share the store and logger without globals. `HTTPServer`
13	  applies the listen address and the read/write timeouts.

## Request flow: `main` → store

1. **`cmd/svc/main.go`** — `main` calls `config.Load()` to read env vars, creates a `store.NewMemStore()`, then wires both into `server.New(cfg, st, logger)`. Finally it calls `srv.HTTPServer().ListenAndServe()`.

2. **`config/config.go`** — `Load` reads `SVC_ADDR`, `SVC_DB`, `SVC_LOG_LEVEL` (falling back to `Defaults`) and calls `Validate`. The resulting `Config` is passed to the server.

3. **`server/server.go`** — `HTTPServer()` builds an `http.Server` with the configured listen address and 10 s read/write timeouts. `Handler()` creates a `ServeMux` with Go 1.22 method+path patterns and wraps it in the `logged` middleware (which uses a `statusRecorder` to capture the status code and log one line per request).

4. **`server/handlers.go`** — The mux dispatches to `listItems`, `createItem`, `getItem`, or `deleteItem`. Each handler decodes the request, calls the appropriate method on `s.store`, and writes a JSON response via `writeJSON` / `writeError`. Store errors are mapped to HTTP statuses (`ErrNotFound` → 404, `ErrExists` → 409, else 500).

5. **`store/store.go`** — `MemStore` (a `sync.RWMutex`-guarded `map[string]Item`) implements the `Store` interface (`Put`, `Get`, `List`, `Delete`). Items are copied in/out so callers can't mutate stored state.

**Files involved:** `cmd/svc/main.go`, `config/config.go`, `server/server.go`, `server/handlers.go`, `store/store.go`.
